question: Tell me about your FoodSafety RAG project.
answer: I built and deployed FoodSafety RAG, an application that answers food-safety questions using 12 USDA documents. I experimented with different chunking strategies and compared BM25 keyword retrieval, vector search, hybrid retrieval and reranking. My best experiment achieved 16 out of 16 retrieval hits on a curated 16-question evaluation set, with an MRR of 0.964 after experimental Groq reranking. The deployed application uses 109 AI-written passages, OpenAI embeddings, keyword/hybrid retrieval and Groq answer generation. The Groq reranking experiment is not part of the live application.

question: What experience do you have with RAG and retrieval evaluation?
answer: I built a RAG application using USDA food-safety documents and Chroma. I compared 500-character, 1,000-character, section-based and AI-written passages. I tested BM25, vector retrieval, hybrid retrieval, cross-encoder reranking and experimental Groq reranking. I used a curated set of 16 questions to measure retrieval hits and Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR). This helped me understand how chunking, retrieval strategy and ranking affect the relevance of retrieved information.

question: How do you approach AI reliability and evaluation?
answer: I believe an AI application needs to be evaluated beyond whether it produces a fluent answer. In my FoodSafety RAG project, I evaluated retrieval separately from answer quality, using retrieval hits and MRR, and also examined answer accuracy, completeness and relevance. I explored strict source-sentence matching and found it could reject correct answers because of minor formatting differences. This taught me to consider retrieval quality, source grounding and answer verification as separate problems.

The application includes a React merchant dashboard, Wix Bookings webhooks, scheduled email delivery through cron, Resend integration, open and click tracking, and subscription tiers using Wix billing APIs. question: Tell me about Share a Book.
answer: Share a Book is a free Progressive Web App I built to help Pakistani school parents give away or sell used textbooks within their school communities. It uses React, Vite, Tailwind CSS and Firebase Authentication, Firestore and Storage. Features include phone OTP login, parent onboarding, book listings, filtering, photo uploads, WhatsApp contact, reporting and admin functionality. It uses a client-side architecture with Firebase Security Rules rather than a custom API server. One technical challenge was handling mobile photo uploads, including HEIC images and large Android camera files.

question: Tell me about your ClickUp → TopTracker Invoicer.
answer: I built a personal Python automation tool that fetches time entries from ClickUp and transfers them into TopTracker as manual time entries. It then creates a draft invoice. I used the ClickUp REST API and Playwright to automate TopTracker's browser interface because the required invoice and time-entry APIs are not publicly available. It supports dry-run and invoice-only modes. Importantly, it saves drafts only; I review and submit invoices manually.
